question: A car moves with uniform speed along a straight road. Its distance–time graph is:

options.text: a straight line parallel to the time-axis
a straight line inclined to the time-axis

solution:
The correct answer is __**a straight line inclined to the time-axis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Uniform speed** is defined as the condition where an object covers **equal distances** in **equal intervals of time**, regardless of how small these time intervals may be.
 
• In a **distance-time graph**, the **time** is usually represented on the **x-axis** (independent variable) and the **distance** is represented on the **y-axis** (dependent variable).
 
• For an object moving with **uniform speed**, the distance traveled is **directly proportional** to the time elapsed ($s \propto t$). This mathematical relationship results in a **straight line** when plotted on a graph.
 
• The **slope** (gradient) of a distance-time graph represents the **speed** of the moving object. Since the car is moving with **uniform speed**, the slope remains **constant** throughout the motion, which is the characteristic of an **inclined straight line**. ***Hence, the correct answer is a straight line inclined to the time-axis.***
